title: SSO interop with real IdPs: OIDC IdP-initiated sign-in cannot work with Okta, SAML name/email attributes are not mappable (Okta `name` and Entra's URI claims are ignored), and a SAML certificate mismatch is still "Invalid SAML response"
body:
## Edition / version
ObjectOS Enterprise, cloud `main` `de8d979` (framework pin `e24136c2`, which carries #30965, #30966 and #30967's fixes), `@better-auth/sso` 1.7.12. Live Okta developer org; found in objectstack-ai/cloud#3666.

## 1. OIDC IdP-initiated sign-in does not work with Okta
#30967 made a callback with a `code` and no `state` restart the flow (`bounceIfIdpInitiated`). Okta never sends that:
- `idp_initiated_login.mode = OKTA` pushes an ID token through the implicit flow: the tile answers `400 unsupported_response_type` ("Configured response types: [code]").
- `mode = SPEC` (OIDC Core §4, third-party-initiated login) redirects the browser to `initiate_login_uri` with `iss` (+ `target_link_uri`) and **no code**. With `initiate_login_uri = …/sso/callback/okta-oidc`, ObjectOS answered `?error=state_not_found`.

Expected: a third-party-initiated login door. On a request carrying `iss` for a registered provider (and `allowIdpInitiated` on), start the normal SP-initiated flow. The user already has an IdP session, so it is seamless. Entra ID's OIDC "My Apps" launch also opens the app's home or login URL instead of sending a code, so the same door serves it.

SAML IdP-initiated works: with `allowIdpInitiated` on, the Okta SAML tile signed the user in; with it off, the request was refused (and logged, see the UX card for the silent page).

## 2. SAML name and email attributes cannot be mapped
The Register SAML Provider form maps only the groups attribute. The vendor's defaults are email = attribute `email`, else NameID; name = `givenName` + `surname`, else `displayName`, else NameID. Okta was configured with attributes `email`, `name`, `groups`. The JIT user's name became `objectos-test3@example.com` (the NameID), while OIDC in the same org mapped "ObjectOS Test1" correctly. Entra ID's default SAML claims are URIs (`http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/ws/2005/05/identity/claims/givenname`, `…/surname`, `…/emailaddress`), so with no mapping every Entra SAML user is named after their NameID.

Expected: the SAML form (and an edit action) exposes the email / first name / last name / display name attribute mapping (`mapping.email`, `firstName`, `lastName`, `name`), with presets or hints for Entra's URI claim names.

## 3. SAML signature/certificate mismatch is still opaque
After Okta rotated the SAML signing certificate, the ACS answered `?error=saml_error&error_description=Invalid SAML response`, and the server logged only `SAML response validation failed`. #30965 ("every OIDC and SAML refusal answers one opaque error") is closed; OIDC refusals now name their cause, but this SAML one still does not. An admin cannot tell "the IdP's signing certificate does not match the one configured" from any other failure.
